newsitem.title: USA: Inflation still under control -- Dallas Fed's McTeer.
newsitem.headline: Inflation still under control -- Dallas Fed's McTeer.

text.p: Inflation has picked up a little bit recently, but is still mainly under control, Dallas Federal Reserve Bank President Robert McTeer said on Thursday.
"Inflation is still primarily under pretty good control," he told a conference sponsored by the Dallas Fed and the Small Corporate Offering Registration group.
McTeer said inflation indicators, such as commodity prices, turned down several months ago.
And while wages and employee compensation have been rising faster than productivity, pushing up unit labor costs, that has so far not translated into big price rises, he said.

McTeer contrasted the situation now with that in 1994, when the Fed embarked on a series of interest rate increases. Rates then were lower than they are now and there was a "lot of inflation in the pipeline," he said.
While inflation is mainly under control now, it should be lower, according to McTeer. "It's not low enough," he said.
He told his audience that the power of the Fed was sometimes overstated. "Monetary policy is very important but so are a lot of other things," he said.
"We certainly don't have any dials we can dial up the perfect economy. Although, in these days, in one respect, we do have almost a perfect economy," he said.
"We've been operating at pretty well maximum capacity," the Fed official added.
